learning_outcomes.text: After completing the module "Electrical Power Engineering", students will have detailed knowledge of the concepts for the use, transport, and distribution of electrical energy as well as their possible uses and applications. They can compare the essential mechanisms and components of electrical power engineering and evaluate them with regard to their intended use. They are able to distinguish individual systems of electrical installations and make evidence-based, qualitative, and quantitative judgments about their use.

Within the module, students analyze technical problems of electrical power engineering against the background of the decentralization of electrical energy supply. Students can describe relevant electrical engineering problems, develop solutions, and transfer them in an application-oriented manner. The graduates of the module realize the tasks within the framework of the energy transition and thus transfer the content into real implementation scenarios and boundary conditions.

After completing the module "Electrical Power Engineering", students know essential constellations of transport and distribution systems and are able to evaluate them with regard to possible applications and their efficiency. The entire supply and utilization chain of electrical energy is at the center of this. The mechanisms and challenges of the electrical energy transition require new ways of looking at and developing new solutions in the area of distribution and use of electrical energy. The graduates of this module can evaluate the potential of different generation and transport technologies and design suitable systems. Students are able to interpret currently necessary adjustments to power generation. Students understand the different procedures for the provision, distribution or transport and use of electrical energy and select the appropriate procedure for the respective application. With regard to the different and diverse projects for the energy transition, the graduates contribute to the development of solution options.

Students can present and communicate questions about electrical systems. They are competent discussion partners for questions from the field of electrical power engineering in particular and the heat transition in general.

After completing the module, students understand the different boundary conditions for analyzing technical systems for the use and provision of electrical energy. They evaluate suitable components and systems as well as suitable applications with regard to technical and societal challenges, develop solutions and justify their implementation.

syllabus_topics: Electrotechnical components of a power plant
assessment_rules: The graded examination is a written exam. The duration and scope of the exam are specified in the current study regulations.
